# LS-12 Sanitary Lift Station: Control Narrative

**Rev A, draft for Process and Operations review. Not for construction.**
Module: LS12. Requirement IDs: FR-LS12-NNN. Setpoint IDs: SP-NN. Tag names are proposed and must match the instrument index.

**Read first.** Your request leaves 12 values undefined: lag stop level, lag speed, anti-short-cycle timers, start stagger, restart hold, bad-PV limits, and generator pump limit. I did not invent them. They appear as TBD in the setpoint list (Section 12) and as open items (Section 10). The integrator cannot finish programming, and FAT cannot finish, until they are set. Three of the open items are design risks, listed first in Section 10:

- Only 0.5 m separates the high level alarm from the overflow to the creek.
- LSHH-121 sits 0.2 m below the overflow.
- The behavior when LIT-121 fails depends on LSHH-121 alone.

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

LS-12 lifts sanitary sewage from the wet well to the discharge line. Two pumps run on VFDs, and each pump is sized for 100% duty. The PLC controls the pumps by level.

| Interface | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Gravity inlet | Upstream | Raw sewage inflow. Inflow is not controlled. |
| Discharge line | Downstream | Pump discharge. Tag to be confirmed. |
| Central SCADA | Bidirectional | Licensed radio. Monitoring and alarms only. Not required for control. |
| Overflow to creek | Not intended | Overflow is a permit violation. Prevention is the main design goal. |

## 2. Equipment and tags

Full data is in the instrument index. Do not copy it here.

| Tag | Function |
|---|---|
| P-121, P-122 | Submersible pumps |
| VFD-121, VFD-122 | Pump drives |
| HS-121, HS-122 | Hand-Off-Auto switches at the MCC |
| LIT-121 | Level transmitter, range per SP-14 |
| LSL-121 | Low level float |
| LSHH-121 | High-high level float |
| ATS-12, GEN-12 | Transfer switch and standby generator |
| PLC-12 | Station PLC and radio |

## 3. States and transitions (ISA-106)

| State | Name | Entry condition | Level of automation |
|---|---|---|---|
| ST-1 | Unavailable | No pump available | Automatic. Operator resets faults. |
| ST-2 | Standby | At least one pump available, LIT-121 valid, level below SP-01 | Automatic |
| ST-3 | Lead pumping | Level at or above SP-01 | Automatic |
| ST-4 | Lead and lag pumping | Level at or above SP-03 | Automatic |
| ST-5 | Float backup | LIT-121 bad | Automatic entry. Operator reset to exit. |
| ST-6 | Restart hold | PLC power-up or source transfer | Automatic |
| ST-7 | High-high override | LSHH-121 active | Automatic |

A pump is *available* when its HOA switch is in AUTO, it has no latched fault, and VFD-12x reports ready.

| ID | From → To | Condition | Initiator | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-001 | ST-1 → ST-2 | At least one pump is available. | Auto / operator (fault reset) | Set HOA to AUTO, reset fault. Confirm state. |
| FR-LS12-002 | ST-2 → ST-3 | LIT-121 is at or above SP-01 for SP-15. | Auto | Inject level. Confirm lead start. |
| FR-LS12-003 | ST-3 → ST-4 | LIT-121 is at or above SP-03 for SP-15, and a second pump is available. | Auto | Inject level. Confirm lag start. |
| FR-LS12-004 | ST-4 → ST-3 | LIT-121 is at or below SP-10. | Auto | Lower level. Confirm lag stop. |
| FR-LS12-005 | ST-3, ST-4 → ST-2 | LIT-121 is at or below SP-02, or LSL-121 is active. | Auto | Lower level. Trip LSL-121 in a separate test. |
| FR-LS12-006 | ST-2, ST-3, ST-4 → ST-5 | LIT-121 is bad (Section 8). | Auto | Fail the signal. Confirm state. |
| FR-LS12-007 | ST-5 → ST-2 | LIT-121 is valid and the operator pushes RESET. | Operator | Restore the signal. Confirm no exit without RESET. |
| FR-LS12-008 | ST-2 to ST-5 → ST-7 | LSHH-121 is active. | Auto | Trip LSHH-121 in each source state. |
| FR-LS12-009 | ST-7 → ST-4 (or ST-5 if LIT-121 is bad) | LSHH-121 is clear. | Auto | Clear LSHH-121. Confirm state. |
| FR-LS12-010 | Any → ST-6 | PLC-12 powers up, or ATS-12 changes source. | Auto | Cycle PLC power. Operate ATS-12. |
| FR-LS12-011 | ST-6 → ST-2, 3, 4 or 7 | SP-17 has elapsed. The PLC selects the state from current level and floats. | Auto | Restart at low, mid, and high level. |
| FR-LS12-012 | Any → ST-1 | No pump is available. | Auto | Set both HOA to OFF. |

## 4. Regulatory control

One loop: lead pump speed against wet well level. It is a level-to-speed curve, not PID. Tuning values are not part of this narrative.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-013 | PV is LIT-121. Output is the speed reference to the lead pump VFD. The action is direct: speed rises as level rises. | Step the level. Record the speed reference. |
| FR-LS12-014 | The lead speed reference rises linearly from SP-08 at SP-01 to SP-09 at SP-03. Below SP-01 it holds at SP-08. Above SP-03 it holds at SP-09. | Inject five level points. Compare to the formula. |
| FR-LS12-015 | When level falls, the speed reference follows the same curve and holds at SP-08 until SP-02. | Lower the level in steps. Compare to the formula. |
| FR-LS12-016 | The lag pump runs at SP-11. | Start the lag pump. Read the reference. |
| FR-LS12-017 | In ST-7 every running pump runs at SP-09. | Trip LSHH-121. Read both references. |
| FR-LS12-018 | In ST-5 the lead pump runs at SP-12. | Fail LIT-121. Read the reference. |

Cascade and override are not used. Loss of PV is handled in Section 8.

## 5. Sequences (SqBC)

A "none" entry in the Timeout column means the step waits for level. These steps have no timeout by design.

**SQ-1 Lead pump start**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Select the lead pump from the alternation index. | Level reaches SP-01 (FR-LS12-002). | None | None |
| 2 | Check the start permissives: pump available, SP-13 elapsed, start count below SP-16. | All true. | SP-14 | Select the other pump. If none, go to ST-1 and raise the alarm. |
| 3 | Send the run command at the curve speed. | VFD run feedback is true. | SP-18 | Remove the command. Latch pump fault. Go to step 2 with the other pump. |
| 4 | Run. | Level at or below SP-02, or LSL-121 active (go to SQ-3). | None | Run feedback lost: latch pump fault. Start the other pump through SQ-1. |

**SQ-2 Lag pump start**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Select the other pump. | Level at or above SP-03 for SP-15. | None | None |
| 2 | Check the start permissives. | All true. | SP-14 | Raise the lag-unavailable alarm. Keep the lead pump at SP-09. |
| 3 | Send the run command at SP-11. | VFD run feedback is true. | SP-18 | Remove the command. Latch pump fault. Raise the alarm. |
| 4 | Run. | Level at or below SP-10 (go to SQ-3 for the lag pump only). | None | Run feedback lost: latch pump fault. |

**SQ-3 Pump stop**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Remove the run command. | Command removed. | None | None |
| 2 | Verify that run feedback is false. | Feedback false. | SP-19 | Raise the fail-to-stop alarm. Latch pump fault. |
| 3 | Start the SP-13 off timer. | Timer started. | None | None |
| 4 | If all pumps are stopped, swap the lead assignment (FR-LS12-019). | Swap done. | None | None |

**SQ-4 Restart after power loss or transfer**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hold all pumps stopped. | SP-17 elapsed. | SP-17 | None |
| 2 | Read LIT-121, LSL-121, and LSHH-121. | LIT-121 valid. | SP-18 | Go to ST-5. |
| 3 | Start the pumps that current level requires. Separate starts by SP-14. Obey FR-LS12-027. | Pumps match the level. | SP-18 per pump | Apply the SQ-1 failure response. |

## 6. Interlocks and permissives

The cause-and-effect chart CE-LS12 (number TBD) holds the logic. Do not copy it here.

| ID | Function |
|---|---|
| IL-LS12-01 | Low level pump stop from LSL-121 (FR-LS12-005) |
| IL-LS12-02 | High-high pump start from LSHH-121 (FR-LS12-008) |
| IL-LS12-03 | Pump stop on VFD fault or motor protection trip |

FR-LS12-020: CE-LS12 shall contain IL-LS12-01 to IL-LS12-03. Test: document review and one functional test per interlock.

No SIS function is defined here. If overflow prevention is assigned to an SIS, see the SRS and open item OI-01.

## 7. Alarms

The rationalized alarm database ADB-LS12 holds priority, setpoint, and response. FR-LS12-021: ADB-LS12 shall contain an entry for each event below. Test: document review and one trigger test per alarm.

- High level (SP-04)
- LSHH-121 active
- LSL-121 active
- LIT-121 bad
- LIT-121 and float disagreement
- Pump fault (by cause)
- Pump fail-to-start and fail-to-stop
- Lag unavailable
- No pump available
- Generator source active
- Utility power lost
- PLC restart
- SCADA comms loss

## 8. Abnormal handling

| ID | Condition | Detection | Response | Restore | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-022 | LIT-121 bad | Signal outside SP-20 limits, or float disagreement per FR-LS12-023 | Go to ST-5. The lead pump starts on LSHH-121 and runs at SP-12 until LSL-121. | Operator RESET after the signal is valid | Fail the signal low, high, and open. |
| FR-LS12-023 | Float and LIT disagree | LSHH-121 active while LIT-121 is below SP-05 minus SP-21, or LSL-121 active while LIT-121 is above SP-06 plus SP-21 | Raise the alarm. Both floats stay in force. | Operator RESET | Simulate each case. |
| FR-LS12-024 | SCADA comms loss | No poll for SP-22 | Control continues locally. Raise the local alarm. | Automatic | Disconnect the radio. Confirm normal pumping. |
| FR-LS12-025 | Utility power loss | ATS-12 status | Pumps stop. PLC-12 stays powered (see OI-07). After transfer go to ST-6. | Same on re-transfer | Operate ATS-12 at low and high level. |
| FR-LS12-026 | PLC power loss | Hardware | Run commands drop out and pumps stop. Retained data: alternation index, latched faults. | Power-up goes to ST-6. | Cycle power. Confirm retention. |
| FR-LS12-027 | Generator source | ATS-12 source status | The PLC runs no more than SP-23 pumps. | Utility source | Run with the limit. Confirm the lag pump waits. |
| FR-LS12-028 | VFD comms loss (if networked) | Heartbeat | Latch pump fault. | Operator RESET | Pull the network cable. |

## 9. Operator interface

| Item | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-029 | The operator sees level trend, pump status, HOA position, lead pump, source (utility or generator), state, and active alarms. | Inspect screens. |
| FR-LS12-030 | The operator can reset latched pump faults and the ST-5 latch. Setpoint changes need engineer access. | Test each reset and the access level. |
| FR-LS12-031 | No operator prompt is needed for normal operation. | Run a full cycle without input. |

Operations signs off on the states and prompts before FAT.

### Pump alternation and fault logic

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-019 | A pumping cycle ends when all pumps are stopped. At the end of each cycle the lead assignment swaps to the other available pump. | Run four cycles. Confirm P-121, P-122, P-121, P-122. |
| FR-LS12-032 | If only one pump is available, it is the lead pump. Alternation resumes when both are available. | Set one HOA to OFF. Run two cycles. |
| FR-LS12-033 | The alternation index survives PLC power loss. | Cycle PLC power. Confirm the index. |
| FR-LS12-034 | The PLC starts a pump only when its HOA switch is in AUTO. In HAND or OFF the pump is unavailable. | Test each HOA position. |
| FR-LS12-035 | SP-13 and SP-16 do not delay a start when level is at or above SP-03 or LSHH-121 is active. | Trip the level during the off timer. |
| FR-LS12-036 | A latched fault on one pump starts the other pump in its place. | Fault the lead pump while running. |

Decide whether LSHH-121 must start the pumps through hardwiring that bypasses the PLC. Decide whether a permit-driven independent layer is needed. | Process | 2026-11-01 |

## Status against the pre-issue checks

- **Met:** IDs and test methods are assigned. Values are in the list and not in prose. Interlocks, alarms, and SIS are referenced, not restated. Sequences have timeouts and failure responses. Abnormal cases are covered. Open items have owners and dates.
- **Not met:** SP-10 to SP-24 are TBD, so the narrative cannot be tested end to end. The STE pass is partial: sentence length and active voice are applied, but I did not check against the approved dictionary.
- **Not done:** I did not check the tag names against an instrument index, because none was provided.
